$comment: Real-world styles served by real tile providers. These are not fixtures: nobody here controls what they contain, which is the entire point. A finding against one of these is either a real contract break in production or a false positive in the checker, and telling those two apart is what this corpus is for.

targets.notes: Production style, no API key. Vector source via TileJSON plus a raster source. 111 layers.
MapLibre's own demo style. Only 8 layers, but carries an inline GeoJSON source and no sprite, which exercises paths the other targets do not.
324 layers, tiles[] array source rather than TileJSON, and the array form of `sprite` introduced for multi-sprite styles.
Key-gated provider. Expected to produce incomplete checks rather than findings when requests are refused; that is the assertion this target exists to make.

gaps: No PMTiles target yet. The real candidate is the Protomaps v4 planet archive at https://demo-bucket.protomaps.com/v4.pmtiles, which serves range requests, paired with a style generated by @protomaps/basemaps. That needs a new devDependency, so it is deliberately not in this first pass.
No MBTiles target. MBTiles is a local-file format, so a real-world target means shipping or building a real archive rather than fetching one.
